exposure: COVID-19 vaccination status (vaccinated vs. infected after vaccination)
outcome: Maternal anti-spike IgG antibody levels at delivery
Cord blood anti-spike IgG antibody levels at delivery
cohort: The study included 68 pregnant women, divided into two groups: 34 vaccinated women and 34 women infected with COVID-19 after vaccination.
finding: Cord anti-spike IgG levels were positively correlated with maternal anti-spike IgG levels in both groups, and the vaccinated group showed a trend of higher maternal and cord blood antibody levels and antibody transfer ratio to the fetus compared to the infected after vaccination group.
birth_weight: Birth weight was significantly different between the two groups (3.0 +/- 0.3 kg for vaccinated group vs. 2.7 +/- 0.7 kg for infected after vaccination group, p < 0.05).
